content.en: Treeless, circumpolar high-latitude and high-altitude biomes characterized by short growing seasons, extreme subzero winter temperatures, and permanently frozen subsoil (Permafrost).
content.hi: Treeless, circumpolar high-latitude and high-altitude biomes characterized by short growing seasons, extreme subzero winter temperatures, and permanently frozen subsoil (Permafrost).

content.en:
• Arctic Tundra: Encircles the North Pole across Siberia, northern Canada, and Scandinavia; low annual precipitation (< 25 cm, polar desert).
• Alpine Tundra: Found at high mountain elevations above the tree line across the world (including High Himalayas).
• Permafrost: Soil or rock remaining at or below 0°C for at least two consecutive years. Active layer (top 10-100 cm) thaws during brief 50-day summer, creating bogs and wetlands.
• Flora & Fauna: Lichens (Reindeer moss), mosses, sedges, dwarf birches, lemmings, Arctic fox, caribou. No deep-rooted trees due to permafrost barrier.
• Climate Threat: Permafrost thawing releases vast quantities of trapped methane and CO2, driving severe climate feedback loops.

question.en: Why are tall, deep-rooted trees completely absent in the Tundra biome?
question.hi: Why are tall, deep-rooted trees completely absent in the Tundra biome?

text.en: High soil salinity prevents water absorption
text.hi: High soil salinity prevents water absorption

text.en: Permafrost layer prevents root penetration and growing season is too short
text.hi: Permafrost layer prevents root penetration and growing season is too short

text.en: Absence of sunlight throughout the entire year
text.hi: Absence of sunlight throughout the entire year

explanation.en: The permanently frozen subsoil (permafrost) prevents roots from penetrating deep into the ground, and the short summer growing season (50-60 days) does not provide enough warmth for arborescent tree growth.
explanation.hi: The permanently frozen subsoil (permafrost) prevents roots from penetrating deep into the ground, and the short summer growing season (50-60 days) does not provide enough warmth for arborescent tree growth.
